etymology: Hebrew leshem, of uncertain meaning, perhaps “a precious stone” or “jacinth,” the town that the tribe of Dan took and renamed Dan after their father.
biblical_def: Leshem was a town in the far north that the children of Dan went up to take when the coast first allotted to them proved too strait, and the Amorites pressed them into the mountain so that the lot of their inheritance fell short. The principle to recover is the faithfulness of God in the least things, who numbered even this obscure town among the two and twenty cities of Asher. The saint who feels his place small or unknown may remember Ummah, a name spoken but once in Scripture, yet written for ever in the book of God’s faithful dividing of the land, and may rest in the same sovereign hand that set the bounds of his habitation.

etymology: Hebrew chereth, perhaps “a thicket” or “a forest,” the wood in the land of Judah whither David came at the word of the prophet Gad.
biblical_def: Hareth was a forest in the land of Judah whither David came when he fled from Saul and was made to leave the hold by the word of the LORD. The prophet Gad said unto David, Abide not in the hold; depart, and get thee into the land of Judah. Then David departed, and came into the forest of Hareth (1Sa 22:5). It was a wild and wooded place, a shelter for the anointed but yet uncrowned king in the days of his affliction, when he was hunted as a partridge upon the mountains. The dictionary does not labour the obscure points of its situation; what it honours is that the LORD led His servant by the mouth of His prophet even into a forest, ordering the very hiding places of the man after His own heart. The bounds of David’s wandering were set by the same God who divided to the nations their inheritance and determined the bounds of their habitation (Deu 32:8; Act 17:26). Hareth stands as a witness that the LORD is present with His servant in the wild and lonely place, that He directs his steps by His word, and that no forest is so dark that His providence does not appoint and keep the path of him whom He has chosen.

etymology: Hebrew charosheth, “a cutting” or “a workshop of wood,” the seat of Sisera, captain of Jabin’s host, called Harosheth of the Gentiles.
biblical_def: Harosheth, called Harosheth of the Gentiles, was the seat of Sisera, captain of the host of Jabin king of Canaan, who mightily oppressed the children of Israel twenty years, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron (Jdg 4:2). From Harosheth Sisera gathered his chariots and all his people to the river Kishon, when Deborah and Barak went up against him; and from Harosheth the LORD discomfited Sisera and all his chariots before Barak, so that there was not a man left. Sisera fled away on his feet and perished by the hand of Jael, while his host was pursued unto Harosheth of the Gentiles, and all the host of Sisera fell upon the edge of the sword (Jdg 4:16). The dictionary does not labour the obscure points of its situation; what it honours is that the LORD brought down the proud seat of the oppressor and delivered His people by the hand of a woman. The bounds of the nations and the rise and fall of their strongholds are alike in the hand of the God who divided to the nations their inheritance (Deu 32:8; Act 17:26). Harosheth stands as a witness that the LORD overthrows the chariots of the mighty and saves His people when they cry unto Him.
